key_insight: Photonic variational circuits are trainable when the measured observable has low enough variance complexity, making sample cost polynomial for fixed-order photon-number observables but exponential for high-order or probability-based observables.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical design rule for near-term photonic quantum algorithms: choose observables and readout schemes that preserve polynomial sample complexity to make optimization feasible at scale.
method: Defined trainability using the ratio of sample variance to circuit variance to estimate samples needed for loss/gradient resolution.
Analyzed passive linear-optical circuits with photon-number observables to separate trainable and non-trainable regimes.
Identified observable families, including neural-network-based readouts, that enable efficient processing and potential quantum speed-up over classical methods.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytic support plus numerical evidence that circuit variance decays polynomially, leading to polynomial sampling for fixed-order photon-number polynomials and exponential sampling for high-order or output-probability observables.
watch_item: The favorable scaling depends strongly on the observable and measurement model, so practical implementations may still face high sampling overhead outside the identified trainable regime.
paper_title: The trainability of photonic quantum circuits
